newsitem.title: USA: Asarco, Kaiser earnings hurt by low metal prices.
newsitem.headline: Asarco, Kaiser earnings hurt by low metal prices.

text.p: Asarco Inc. and Kaiser Aluminum Corp. Wednesday reported weak fourth-quarter earnings, hurt by lower prices for copper and aluminum.

Asarco, one of the nation's biggest copper producers, said net earnings were $24.3 million, or 57 cents a share, for the quarter, compared with a loss of $11.3 million, or 27 cents a share, for the 1995 quarter.
But excluding a charge of $79.5 million from the 1995 quarter, operating earnings fell in the latest quarter, hurt by a 25 percent drop in copper prices, the company said.
Sales fell to $651.5 million from $799.6 million. New York-based Asarco also produces lead, zinc, molybdenum and silver.

"The lower copper prices resulted in the decline in Asarco's earnings in the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with the fourth quarter of 1995, before the special charge recorded in the year-earlier period," Chairman Richard de J. Osborne said in a statement.
The drop in copper prices to about 99 cents a pound in the quarter from $1.32 a pound a year earlier cut earnings by about $43 million in the quarter, the company said.
For the year, Asarco earned $138.3 million, or $3.24 a share, compared with $169.2 million, or $4 a share, in 1995.
Sales fell to $2.70 billion from $3.20 billion.

Houston-based Kaiser, an aluminum producer, reported a net loss of $3.3 million, or 8 cents a share, for the quarter, compared to profits of $21 million, or 26 cents a share, in the 1995 period. The latest results include a gain of $17 million, or 24 cents a share, from tax adjustments.

Excluding the tax adjustments, "the company's results were unfavourable compared to those of the year-ago period" mostly because of lower prices for aluminum and fabricated products, Chairman George Haymaker Jr. said in a statement.
Results were also hurt by high energy costs and expenses for maintenance at its Trentwood, Wash., rolling mill.
Sales fell 9 percent to $538.4 million from $591.1 million.

For the year, Kaiser earned $8.2 million, or nil on a per share basis, compared to net income of $60.3 million, or 69 cents a share, for 1995. Sales dropped 2 percent to $2.19 billion from $2.24 billion.
Asarco stock rose 50 cents to $27.50, and Kaiser was unchanged at $13.25, both in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
